annotations.title: Check up to fifty addresses in one call (paid)

description: Check up to fifty addresses in one call, each with its observations, AND what the set shares underneath: the parties that two or more of them pay. That second part is the one answer no per-address row can contain, because the input is your own shortlist — four agents stopping together because they all pay one party is invisible in four separate clean records. PAID two ways and they buy different things: one cent a call over x402, priced per call rather than per address, buys the rows; the `shared` block needs the `dependency.shared` capability, on Analyst and above, and when it is missing the block says so rather than vanishing. A shared recipient is not proof of a shared dependency — several agents paying one address may be paying a relayer, a bridge or the same customer back — and an empty list is a finding about these addresses AND about our reach. WHY readOnlyHint IS false: this tool reads and writes nothing in our store, but calling it WITH an x402 payment authorisation transfers USDC from the caller to us and records a receipt, so the call is not free of consequence and an agent must not make it speculatively. Called without an authorisation it changes nothing and answers with the price.

payment.description: What was paid and how it settled. Priced per call, not per address.

shared.description: The parties two or more of the given addresses pay, most shared first, each with how many of yours pay it and which ones. `available: false` with a `capability` name where the plan does not carry it. An empty list means no party is paid by more than one of them on a rail we read, which is a finding about them and about our reach: a model, an endpoint or a host shared between them is a dependency no payment rail shows.
